item.title: #3589894: Remove the archive, glossary and recent content block views
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 21 files, +188/−129 · php +173/−119 · yml +15/−10
  • Diff: b5c577d
  • Discussion: #3589894 · 4 contributors · 21 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Node module used to ship three disabled-by-default Views: an Archive view (monthly content listing), a Glossary view (alphabetical content listing), and a "Recent content" block view. These assumed a blog-like site, dated back to early Drupal versions, and were not used anywhere in core, yet they still showed up in the Views UI and were parsed on every request. As of this change, new Drupal installs no longer include these three views at all. Sites that want an archive or glossary style listing will need to build their own view or find one in a contributed or example module. Existing sites are not affected since this only changes what ships with new installs; it does not remove views already present in a site's active configuration.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Config change: New sites no longer get the disabled-by-default views.view.archive, views.view.glossary and views.view.content_recent views from node.module's config/optional directory; existing sites that already have them in active config are unaffected.

Technical details

The change deletes core/modules/node/config/optional/views.view.archive.yml, views.view.glossary.yml, and views.view.content_recent.yml outright, and updates core/recipes/standard/recipe.yml to drop views.view.archive and views.view.glossary from its node: config import list (views.view.content_recent remains listed there even though the source config file is gone).

Since core tests exercised these views directly, the same view configs were carried over as test fixtures under new IDs: test_archive (added to views_test_config's test views, with a new ArchiveTest in core/modules/views/tests/src/Functional), test_glossary (added to views_ui_test's config, exercised by GlossaryTest and views_ui's DefaultViewsTest), and test_content_recent (added to node_block_test, used by NodeBlockFunctionalTest). Various other tests that referenced the old archive/glossary/content_recent view or block IDs (ContextualLinksTest, FilterCriteriaTest, ModuleTest, BlockDependenciesTest, ViewsListingTest, InstallerExistingConfigSyncDirectoryMultilingualTest, StandardRecipeTest) were updated to use the new test view IDs or to drop assertions tied to the removed views. A related follow-up, #3592672, removes the "who's new" and "who's online" views in the same spirit.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 13, 2026
  • Committed: August 4, 2026 (2 months later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Third and Grove)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • acbramley (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

catch opened the issue, crediting a Slack discussion with gábor hojtsy about why these blog-oriented views should go. gábor hojtsy did the bulk of the test-adaptation work: he determined that the glossary and archive views had tests validating their actual query/rendering behavior and so needed to survive as dedicated test views rather than just be deleted, and reworked the views_ui DefaultViewsTest, which he described as "the trickiest" because it assumed the glossary view existed and had accumulated some outdated, half-commented-out assertions he cleaned up along the way. acbramley later rebased the patch and fixed further breakage in DefaultViewsTest caused by the unrelated removal of the frontpage view in the interim, tracking down a ViewRenderElementException that turned out to be a local-environment issue rather than a real bug. smustgrave reviewed and flagged remaining references to the removed views in RecipeRunnerTest, InstallerExistingConfigSyncDirectoryMultilingualTest, and a docblock example in ConfigEntityStorageInterface.

item.title: #3607968: Promote defaults._title to top level in route attributes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 17 files, +415/−47 · php +415/−37 · yml +0/−10
  • Diff: c51fe13
  • Discussion: #3607968 · 5 contributors · 33 comments
  • Followers: 6

Summary

Following up on the introduction of PHP attributes for route discovery (#3311365), Drupal core now provides its own #[Route] attribute that extends Symfony's, adding a top level title property. Previously, setting a page title on an attribute-based route required nesting it inside defaults: ['_title' => ...]; now it can be written as title: new TranslatableMarkup('...') directly on the attribute. The new attribute also supports closures for dynamic titles, letting modules avoid writing a separate _title_callback controller method just to compute a title. This is a developer-facing convenience change with no end-user visible effect, aside from the many core routes (system.module's admin pages, block content add form, etc.) that were converted to use it.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: BlockContentController::getAddFormTitle() is deprecated in favor of a title closure on the route attribute.
  • New API: New title property on Drupal's #[Route] attribute (Drupal\Core\Routing\Attribute\Route, extending Symfony's), accepting a string, TranslatableMarkup, or closure for the page title.

Technical details

The new Drupal\Core\Routing\Attribute\Route class extends Symfony\Component\Routing\Attribute\Route and, in its constructor, moves a passed title argument into $this->defaults['_title']. Passing both title and a _title default simultaneously trips an assertion. Because closures cannot be serialized into the router table, AttributeRouteDiscovery::getAttributes() detects a closure title and replaces it in the stored defaults with a _title_closure reference tuple of [class, method, index] (the index disambiguates multiple #[Route] attributes on the same method). TitleResolver::getTitle() was updated to recognize _title_closure and resolve the actual closure at render time via the new static method Route::getTitleClosure(), which re-reflects the method's attributes to retrieve the closure (since it can't be persisted) and resolves controller arguments the same way _title_callback does, except without container access.

All core routes previously using defaults: ['_title' => ...] on attribute-based routes were converted to the top level title property, including the system.module admin controllers and SiteInformationForm. BlockContentController::addForm()'s route was converted to use a closure title (title: static function (BlockContentTypeInterface $block_content_type) {...}), and its old getAddFormTitle() method was deprecated for removal in Drupal 13.0.0, with the accompanying block_content.add_form YAML route definition removed since discovery now happens purely through the attribute.

Upgrade

Modules converting *.routing.yml route definitions to #[Route] attributes (per #3311365) can now write, instead of:

#[Route(
  path: '/admin/config/system/site-information',
  name: 'system.site_information_settings',
  requirements: ['_permission' => 'administer site configuration'],
  defaults: ['_title' => new TranslatableMarkup('Basic site settings')],
)]

the shorter:

#[Route(
  path: '/admin/config/system/site-information',
  name: 'system.site_information_settings',
  title: new TranslatableMarkup('Basic site settings'),
  requirements: ['_permission' => 'administer site configuration'],
)]

For dynamic titles that don't need injected services, a closure can replace a separate _title_callback method:

#[Route(
  path: '/block/add/{block_content_type}',
  name: 'block_content.add_form',
  title: static function (BlockContentTypeInterface $block_content_type) {
    return new TranslatableMarkup('Add %type content block', ['%type' => $block_content_type->label()]);
  },
  requirements: ['_entity_create_access' => 'block_content:{block_content_type}'],
)]

Code calling Drupal\block_content\Controller\BlockContentController::getAddFormTitle() should stop using it before Drupal 13.0.0.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 2, 2026
  • Committed: August 1, 2026 (29 days and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • longwave (Full Fat Things)
  • godotislate
  • mstrelan (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

The design went through several iterations before landing. longwave initially proposed extending the Symfony Route attribute, but also floated an alternative of a separate #[PageTitle] attribute (mirroring how Symfony handles access control via a separate #[IsGranted] attribute). godotislate and mstrelan weighed in on the tradeoffs, and godotislate pointed out the deciding issue: SystemController::systemAdminMenuBlockPage() has several different #[Route] attributes stacked on one method, each needing its own title, which rules out a single class or method level #[PageTitle] attribute since there would be no way to tell which title belongs to which route. This led longwave to add closure support directly to the #[Route] attribute and solve the "which attribute" ambiguity by recording an [class, method, index] reference during route discovery. godotislate reviewed the resulting MR, confirmed the route discovery skip-file logic still worked with the new attribute, and catch merged it, noting it was "soft-blocking a lot of route conversions from YAML."

item.title: #3593472: Insecure Direct Object Reference in Private File Uploads
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.4.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +140/−2 · php +140/−2
  • Diff: 83a5f2b
  • Discussion: #3593472 · 3 contributors · 15 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Fixes a security vulnerability in the file upload widget used by file and image fields. Previously, a logged in user could tamper with the file ID submitted by the upload form (for example by editing the hidden fids input in browser dev tools) and cause another user's private file, one they had no permission to view or download, to be attached to their own content. An attacker did not need to know the file's contents, only its numeric ID, which is easy to guess since file IDs are sequential. Sites using private file storage for file or image fields should update to receive this fix.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in the ManagedFile upload widget allowed a user to attach a private file they do not have download access to (identified only by guessing its fid) to their own content.

Technical details

The fix is in ManagedFile::valueCallback() in core/modules/file/src/Element/ManagedFile.php. When processing newly uploaded files for multi-value widgets, the code now loads all candidate files with File::loadMultiple($fids) and filters out any whose $file->access('download') check fails for the current user, removing those denied fids from the array before they are stored on the field. The same access check was added to the code path that reconstructs $fids from $default_fids (used when redisplaying a form after validation errors or AJAX rebuilds), replacing a bare File::load($fid) existence check with an access('download') check via File::loadMultiple().

A new test, ManagedFileFidValidationTest, exercises this directly: it creates a private, temporary file owned by one user, then logs in as a second user and confirms that submitting a form with the first user's fid injected via the URL (simulating a tampered request) does not result in that fid being accepted, whether or not the second user also performs a legitimate upload in the same request. An existing image test (testDefaultImages) needed a setOwner() call added so its private test images remain accessible to the test's own user under the new check.

  • Committed: July 30, 2026 (1 month and 3 commits later)

item.title: #3584238: Deprecate implicit commit-on-destruct
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +117/−15 · php +117/−15
  • Diff: 9a20b9c
  • Discussion: #3584238 · 6 contributors · 29 comments
  • Followers: 11

Summary

Drupal's database transaction system has, since its inception, committed a transaction automatically when the PHP Transaction object holding it went out of scope and was garbage collected. This implicit "commit on destruct" behavior is now deprecated: code should instead call $transaction->commitOrRelease() explicitly once the wrapped database operations have completed. The old behavior still works for now (it's removed only in Drupal 13.0.0), so most sites and contributed modules will keep working unchanged, but developers writing custom code that opens transactions directly should update it to avoid deprecation notices and to avoid relying on PHP's unpredictable object destruction order. A few internal helper methods added earlier as a workaround for this same destruction-order problem (Connection::commitAll(), Database::commitAllOnShutdown(), TransactionManagerBase::commitAll()) are also deprecated with no replacement, since they exist only to support the mechanism being phased out.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Implicit commit of a Transaction object on destruction is deprecated (removed in Drupal 13.0.0). Also deprecated for removal: Connection::commitAll(), Database::commitAllOnShutdown(), TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(), with no replacement.

Technical details

TransactionManagerBase::purge(), called when a Transaction object's destructor runs, now emits @trigger_error(..., E_USER_DEPRECATED) pointing to Transaction::commitOrRelease() as the replacement, unless a new private $exceptionThrown flag is set. That flag is set whenever push(), unpile(), commit(), rollback(), addPostTransactionCallback(), or processRootCommit() throws (TransactionNameNonUniqueException, TransactionOutOfOrderException, TransactionCommitFailedException, LogicException), so that objects destroyed during exception unwinding don't produce a spurious deprecation notice, and is reset to FALSE whenever a new root transaction begins. TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(), Connection::commitAll(), and Database::commitAllOnShutdown() are marked @deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 ... removed from drupal:13.0.0 using only doc-comment deprecation (no @trigger_error), since these run implicitly on every request shutdown and would otherwise flood deprecation logs; PHPStan (@phpstan-ignore) is relied on instead to catch remaining usages statically.

Separately, ContentEntityStorageBase::save() now catches \Throwable instead of \Exception around the save operation before rolling back its transaction. Per mondrake's comment on the issue, the narrower \Exception catch could let a PHP Error escape without rolling back, leaving the transaction to be released (committed) via destruction instead of rolled back, exactly the kind of bug this deprecation effort is meant to surface and prevent.

Class doc comments on Transaction and Connection were updated to no longer describe destruction-triggered commit as the intended usage pattern, directing developers toward calling commitOrRelease() explicitly instead. See the change record at drupal.org/node/3524461. Related issues #3569127 and #3569316 dealt with fallout from the underlying destruction-order transaction work this deprecation follows up on.

Upgrade

Code that opens a transaction directly and lets it commit implicitly when the variable goes out of scope should call commitOrRelease() explicitly instead:

try {
  $transaction = \Drupal::database()->startTransaction();
  // ... perform database operations ...
  my_other_function($id);

  // The transaction has completed, commit it here.
  $transaction->commitOrRelease();

  return $id;
}
catch (Exception $e) {
  $transaction->rollback();
  throw $e;
}

Do not call Connection::commitAll(), Database::commitAllOnShutdown(), or TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(): they are deprecated with no replacement and will be removed in Drupal 13.0.0.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 11, 2026
  • Committed: July 30, 2026 (3 months and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • mondrake
  • mradcliffe (Kosada)
  • daffie
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

mondrake, who authored the fix, noted mid-review that "another commit-on-destruct has leaked in the code base" and traced a subtle bug: a try/catch(\Exception) in ContentEntityStorageBase::save() failed to intercept a PHP Error, causing a savepoint to be released instead of rolled back. mondrake called this "tough" to track down and said it drove the broader improvement of catching \Throwable there. mradcliffe reviewed the change, manually tested installation under PostgreSQL 18 and checked for performance regressions before marking it RTBC.

item.title: #3050199: Remove entity level constraint MenuSettingsConstraint that validates property only added in a form
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +59/−49 · php +59/−49
  • Diff: 214876b
  • Discussion: #3050199 · 4 contributors · 18 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Drupal previously blocked changes to a node's menu settings (parent, weight, or removing the menu link) while editing a pending, non-default revision by attaching a validation constraint directly to the node entity type. Because that constraint ran on every save of a node, not just form submissions, it could reject unrelated saves made through code that doesn't go through the node edit form, such as JSON API or REST requests, or programmatic saves during content moderation workflows (as reported in #3048698). This entity-level check has been removed. The same protection now runs only as part of the node add/edit form's validation, so saving a node's menu settings through other means, such as web services or custom code, is no longer restricted by this rule.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: MenuSettingsConstraint and MenuSettingsConstraintValidator are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 for removal in drupal:13.0.0; the check they performed moved to MenuUiHooks::formNodeFormValidate().

Technical details

The check lived in MenuSettingsConstraint/MenuSettingsConstraintValidator, added to the node entity type unconditionally in MenuUiHooks::entityTypeBuild(). Since $entity->menu is only populated by menu_ui_node_builder() during a node form submission, the constraint's logic was effectively meaningless outside that context, which is what #3048698 and #3010750 ran into.

The fix drops the $entity_types['node']->addConstraint('MenuSettings', []) call from entityTypeBuild() and moves the equivalent logic into a new MenuUiHooks::formNodeFormValidate() method, registered via $form['#validate'][] inside formNodeFormAlter(). It reads the submitted menu form value plus MenuUiUtility::getMenuLinkDefaults() and calls $form_state->setErrorByName() for the same three cases the old constraint reported: removing a menu link, changing its parent menu, or changing its weight, all while editing a pending revision.

MenuSettingsConstraint and MenuSettingsConstraintValidator remain in the codebase but are marked @deprecated for removal in Drupal 13.0.0 (see https://www.drupal.org/node/3606616); the validator's validate() method now only triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED notice and performs no validation.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Code that explicitly instantiates or extends MenuSettingsConstraint or MenuSettingsConstraintValidator should stop doing so before Drupal 13.0.0, when they will be removed:

/**
 * @deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and is removed from drupal:13.0.0. Menu
 *   settings validation is now handled as a form validation callback in
 *   \Drupal\menu_ui\Hook\MenuUiHooks::formNodeFormValidate().
 */

If your code relies on menu settings for pending revisions being protected outside the node edit form (for example, saves through JSON API, REST, or custom code), add your own validation, since the node entity type no longer carries the MenuSettings constraint.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 23, 2019
  • Committed: July 30, 2026 (7 years and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • tedbow (Acquia)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

smustgrave revisited the issue during queue triage and confirmed the concern was still valid, then opened the MR that converted the entity-level MenuSettingsConstraint into the formNodeFormValidate() form validation handler that shipped.

item.title: #3209204: Adding existing translation throws "Invalid translation language specified"
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.4.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +96/−1 · php +96/−1
  • Diff: e179038
  • Discussion: #3209204 · 13 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 18

Summary

Content editors could get a fatal PHP error ("Invalid translation language specified", a 500 error page) simply by opening the "Add translation" link for a language that had already been translated, for example by clicking it in two browser tabs, or navigating back after saving a translation. This was easy to hit in ordinary editing workflows for both content entities and menu links. The fix makes ContentTranslationController::add() detect that the target translation already exists before building the add form, and instead shows the message "A translation already exists for [language]" and redirects the editor to the existing translation's edit form.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The crash happened because ContentTranslationController::add() unconditionally cloned the entity and called addTranslation() for the target language, which throws an InvalidArgumentException in ContentEntityBase::addTranslation() if that translation already exists. This could occur through races such as two open tabs each adding the same translation, a browser "back" navigation returning to a stale add-translation URL, or another user saving the same translation concurrently.

The fix adds a guard in add(): if $entity->hasTranslation($target->getId()) is true, it calls $this->messenger()->addError() with a translated message and returns a Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse to $entity->getTranslation($target->getId())->toUrl('edit-form')->toString() instead of proceeding to build the form. The method's return type was widened from array to array|\Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation\RedirectResponse to reflect this. A new kernel test, ContentTranslationConcurrencyTest, exercises this by creating an entity with an existing French translation and calling the controller's add() method directly, asserting a redirect response and the error message text.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 16, 2021
  • Committed: July 29, 2026 (5 years and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • trevorbradley
  • randalv
  • johnwebdev
  • dieterholvoet (Minsky)
  • smustgrave (Mobomo)
  • andras_szilagyi (European Commission and European Union Institutions, Agencies and Bodies)
  • claudiu.cristea (Webikon)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

DieterHolvoet revised the fix so that it redirects to the existing translation's edit form rather than back to the translation overview, judging it more user friendly, and confirmed the same fix also resolved the equivalent crash for menu link translations reported by johnwebdev and mpp. Andras Szilagyi later added the kernel test covering the redirect and error message. Claudiu Cristea, investigating a related report of the same error on macOS/Safari, traced an additional trigger: another user saving the same translation concurrently while the current user is still on the add-translation form, which explained why the fix needed to be a defensive check rather than only a client-side navigation issue.

item.title: #3590917: Introduce a common ancestor class to all Core base test classes
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +114/−77 · php +114/−77
  • Diff: fc3581f
  • Discussion: #3590917 · 5 contributors · 17 comments
  • Followers: 7

Summary

Drupal core's PHPUnit test base classes, UnitTestCase, KernelTestBase, BrowserTestBase, and Drupal\BuildTests\Framework\BuildTestBase, now all extend a single common ancestor, Drupal\Tests\DrupalTestCase, instead of each separately extending PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase and using DrupalTestCaseTrait. For the vast majority of unit, kernel, functional, functional-javascript, and build tests in contrib and custom code, which extend one of these existing base classes, nothing changes. The change mainly matters if you write PHPUnit tests for a Drupal\Component library that extend PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase directly (as is required, since Component code must not depend on Core code): if such a test wants Drupal's PHPUnit extensions, it now has to import DrupalTestCaseTrait explicitly rather than getting it automatically.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: The already-deprecated getDrupalRoot() method moved from DrupalTestCaseTrait to DrupalTestCase and lost its static modifier, becoming a regular instance method.
  • New API: New abstract Drupal\Tests\DrupalTestCase class is the common ancestor of UnitTestCase, KernelTestBase, BrowserTestBase and Drupal\BuildTests\Framework\BuildTestBase.

Technical details

Previously, UnitTestCase, KernelTestBase, BrowserTestBase, and BuildTestBase each independently extended PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase and separately used DrupalTestCaseTrait for shared behavior, most notably setting the $root property via a #[Before(100)]-tagged setUpRoot() hook and exposing the deprecated getDrupalRoot() accessor. The new Drupal\Tests\DrupalTestCase abstract class centralizes that: it extends PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase, uses DrupalTestCaseTrait once, and declares the $root property, setUpRoot(), and getDrupalRoot() itself. All four base classes now extend DrupalTestCase instead of TestCase directly, and dropped their own use DrupalTestCaseTrait; statements.

DrupalTestCaseTrait itself was trimmed down to the remaining cross-cutting helpers (such as registering the dumper CLI handler) and re-documented as something you only need to import directly when writing a Drupal\Component test that extends PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase and still wants Drupal's PHPUnit extensions. As part of moving getDrupalRoot() onto DrupalTestCase, it dropped the static modifier it had on the trait, since $this->root is an instance property.

Upgrade

If you maintain a Drupal\Component PHPUnit test that extends PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase directly and relies on Drupal's PHPUnit extensions (previously available for free via DrupalTestCaseTrait), import the trait explicitly:

use Drupal\Tests\DrupalTestCaseTrait;
use PHPUnit\Framework\TestCase;

class MyComponentTest extends TestCase {
  use DrupalTestCaseTrait;
}

Tests that already extend UnitTestCase, KernelTestBase, BrowserTestBase, or BuildTestBase require no changes.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: May 19, 2026
  • Committed: July 29, 2026 (2 months later)

Key contributors

  • mondrake
  • kingdutch (Open Social)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)

Collaboration

kingdutch reviewed the change as a recent contributor to the test scaffolding, noting that tracing properties across the previously separate traits had been difficult, and that the new shared DrupalTestCase base class makes explicit what is minimally needed to test Drupal code. He discussed with mondrake why BuildTestBase still needed its own PHPStan baseline entry for the deprecated getDrupalRoot() call, and pointed to #1792310 and #3590337 as candidates for resolving that inconsistency later. Separately, quietone found the new docblock added to DrupalTestCaseTrait too dense and asked for plain-language wording; mondrake rewrote it, and quietone confirmed the revision was clearer before restoring RTBC.

item.title: #3613344: Remove update_fetch_with_http_fallback
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +14/−317 · php +14/−316 · yml +0/−1
  • Diff: 5a7489d
  • Discussion: #3613344 · 5 contributors · 11 comments
  • Followers: 6

Summary

Drupal 12 removes the update_fetch_with_http_fallback setting, which previously let a site fall back to plain HTTP when HTTPS requests to updates.drupal.org failed while checking for available updates or security advisories. This insecure fallback option was deprecated in Drupal 11.5 (#3591513) and is now gone with no replacement. Sites that still have this setting uncommented in settings.php should remove it; it no longer has any effect and update/security-advisory checks will always use HTTPS.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\update\UpdateFetcher::__construct() and Drupal\Core\Update\SecurityAdvisoriesFetcher::__construct() no longer accept a Settings argument; the internal Drupal\package_manager\Validator\SettingsValidator class and its service definition were removed entirely.
  • Deprecation: The update_fetch_with_http_fallback settings.php setting, deprecated in Drupal 11.5, is removed in Drupal 12 with no replacement.

Technical details

The change strips the update_fetch_with_http_fallback handling out of the two places that read it: Drupal\update\UpdateFetcher::doRequest() and Drupal\Core\Update\SecurityAdvisoriesFetcher::doRequest() (formerly Drupal\system\SecurityAdvisories\SecurityAdvisoriesFetcher) now issue a single HTTPS GET and no longer catch a failed HTTPS attempt to retry over http://. Both classes' constructors drop the injected Settings $settings parameter along with the $withHttpFallback property. The corresponding entry in Drupal\Core\Site\Settings::$deprecatedSettings is removed, leaving that array empty.

Package Manager's Drupal\package_manager\Validator\SettingsValidator, which existed solely to block updates while the fallback setting was enabled, is deleted along with its service definition and SettingsValidatorTest. The commented-out documentation block for the setting is removed from default.settings.php. Test coverage for the HTTP-fallback code paths (testHttpFallback, testUpdateFetcherHttpFallback) was removed accordingly, and Drupal\Tests\Core\Site\SettingsTest::testRealDeprecatedSettings is marked skipped rather than deleted outright, since it needs at least one real "deprecated with no replacement" setting to exercise its data provider and none currently exists for the Drupal 12 transition.</technical> <parameter name="upgrade">Remove any uncommented update_fetch_with_http_fallback line from settings.php; it has no effect on Drupal 12 and update checks always use HTTPS:

# $settings['update_fetch_with_http_fallback'] = TRUE;

If custom code instantiates or extends Drupal\update\UpdateFetcher or Drupal\Core\Update\SecurityAdvisoriesFetcher directly, remove the Settings $settings constructor argument, for example:

item.description:

Summary

CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck, the service that decides which routes need the X-CSRF-Token header check, used an outdated way of detecting which HTTP methods a route allows. It looked for the legacy _method route requirement to decide whether a route was read-only (and could skip the check), but modern routes declare allowed methods with the methods property instead, so that optimization silently never applied to them. This didn't cause a security problem, since the check itself already allows GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE requests, but it meant the check was being unnecessarily evaluated on read-only routes defined the modern way. The fix drops the outdated, partially broken logic and instead declares the check statically for any route that has the _csrf_request_header_token requirement, regardless of how its methods are declared.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Drupal\Core\Access\CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck now implements Drupal\Core\Routing\Access\AccessInterface instead of AccessCheckInterface; its applies(Route $route) method has been removed.

Technical details

Previously CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck implemented AccessCheckInterface, which requires an applies(Route $route) method that Drupal calls dynamically per route to decide whether to attach the checker. That method inspected the deprecated _method route requirement and only skipped attaching the check if all required methods were read-only; routes using the modern methods route property never had _method set, so the method-based skip never kicked in for them.

The fix, following a suggestion from longwood in the thread that the check "doesn't need to be dynamic at all," removes applies() and the _method inspection entirely. CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck now implements the plain AccessInterface and is registered in core.services.yml with applies_to: _csrf_request_header_token on its access_check service tag, so Drupal's CheckProvider attaches it statically based purely on the presence of that requirement key. The actual read/write distinction is still enforced at runtime inside access(), which already unconditionally allows GET, HEAD, OPTIONS and TRACE requests before checking for the CSRF token header. A new kernel test, CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheckTest, asserts the checker is attached to routes declaring _csrf_request_header_token regardless of their declared methods, and not attached when the requirement is absent.

Upgrade

If custom code extends CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck or type-hints against AccessCheckInterface specifically for this class, update to the new contract: implement Drupal\Core\Routing\Access\AccessInterface and rely on the applies_to service tag attribute instead of overriding applies(). For example, in a service definition:

access_check.header.csrf:
  class: Drupal\Core\Access\CsrfRequestHeaderAccessCheck
  arguments: ['@session_configuration', '@csrf_token']
  tags:
    - { name: access_check, applies_to: _csrf_request_header_token, needs_incoming_request: TRUE }

Routes that rely on this checker should also prefer the methods route property over the deprecated _method requirement key.

Summary

Drupal core's development branch (targeting Drupal 12) updates its bundled Symfony components from the 8.0.x series to 8.1.1, along with a matching PHPUnit bump. There is no behavioral change for end users. The practical impact is for developers who write PHPUnit tests: Symfony 8.1 changed how Request and Response expose their public properties (query, request, server, headers), and the old pattern of mocking these classes and assigning those properties directly, which Drupal core's own test suite used extensively, no longer works reliably. Tests need to construct real Request/Response objects instead. Symfony's validator component also deprecates the old ConstraintValidator::initialize()/::validate() methods in favor of validateInContext().

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: Drupal core (main, targeting Drupal 12) now requires symfony/* packages ^8.1 instead of ^8.0, and bumps phpunit/phpunit to ^12.5.15.
  • Deprecation: Symfony 8.1 deprecates directly setting public properties like $response->headers or $request->query on Request/Response/CacheableResponse (now property hooks), and deprecates ConstraintValidator::initialize()/::validate() in favor of validateInContext().

Technical details

The diff bumps version constraints in composer.json/core/composer.json (and the corresponding composer.lock) for symfony/console, dependency-injection, event-dispatcher, filesystem, finder, http-foundation, http-kernel, mailer, mime, process, routing, runtime, serializer, validator, and yaml from ^8.0 to ^8.1, plus dev dependencies (phpunit/phpunit to satisfy sebastianbergmann/phpunit#6545, symfony/browser-kit, css-selector, dom-crawler, error-handler, lock, var-dumper).

item.title: #2951046: Allow parsing and writing PHP class constants and enums in YAML files
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 39 files, +921/−13 · php +835/−11 · yml +86/−2

  • Followers: 58

Summary

Drupal's YAML parser now understands PHP class constants and enum cases, so configuration, service definitions, and recipe files can reference SomeClass::SOME_CONSTANT or SomeEnum::SomeCase instead of hard-coding literal values that have to be kept in sync by hand. A companion enum config schema type lets module authors declare that a config value must be an instance of a specific PHP enum, with validation enforcing it. To make this safe during module installation and config import, when a module or recipe is being installed its enums and constants are made autoloadable even before the module is fully active, so its own default configuration can reference them. Support is deliberately limited to class-based constants and enums; global constants defined in procedural .module files are not supported.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Drupal\Core\Config\FileStorageFactory and its getSync() method are deprecated in favor of the config.storage.sync service.
  • New API: YAML (including configuration, services and recipes) can now contain !php/const Some\Class::CONST and !php/enum Some\Enum::Case tags; a new enum config schema type with an enum_class key validates that a config value is an instance of that enum.

Technical details

The core change is small: Drupal\Component\Serialization\YamlSymfony::decode() now passes SymfonyYaml::PARSE_CONSTANT alongside the existing flags, which enables Symfony's !php/const and !php/enum YAML tags. Yaml::encode() (Symfony writer) serializes PHP enums using !php/const, which the parser also accepts back, and !php/enum is additionally supported on decode for compatibility with Symfony's documented syntax and to keep behavior consistent regardless of which YAML backend is in use.

A new Drupal\Core\TypedData\Plugin\DataType\Enum primitive type (schema id enum) plus EnumConstraint/EnumConstraintValidator validate that a decoded value is a \UnitEnum instance of the class named in the schema's enum_class key; Comparator::checkValue() and TypedConfig::castValue() were updated to recognize \UnitEnum values.

The harder problem was config install/import: enums and constants referenced in a module's or recipe's own default configuration are not autoloadable via Composer until the providing module is installed. This is solved with a new Drupal\Core\Config\AutoloadingStorage decorator that temporarily registers a throwaway ClassLoader (PSR-4 mapped to the extension's src directory) around read()/readMultiple() calls. The config.storage.sync service is now produced by a new SyncFactory class, which diffs the core.extension list in the sync storage against the active storage to find newly-appearing modules/themes and wraps the sync FileStorage in AutoloadingStorage for just those extensions. ModuleInstaller::checkConfigurationToInstall() does the same for the module(s) currently being installed. StorageComparer was updated to treat AutoloadingStorage the same as FileStorage for its static-cache optimization. Recipes get analogous handling: parseRecipeContents() in Drupal\Core\Recipe\RecipeData catches the InvalidDataTypeException Symfony throws for an unresolvable Drupal\{extension}\... constant/enum, and if that extension exists on disk but isn't installed yet, registers a temporary classloader for it and retries parsing.

Support for constants defined in procedural .module files was explicitly dropped rather than solved, since it would require preloading .module files before parsing config, a complication the maintainers decided wasn't worth it for a legacy pattern that's being phased out.

Upgrade

Prefer !php/const and !php/enum over literal values in your own config/service YAML, e.g.:

cardinality: !php/const Drupal\Core\Field\FieldStorageDefinitionInterface::CARDINALITY_UNLIMITED
status: !php/enum Drupal\my_module\MyEnum::SomeCase

Declare a matching config schema for enum-typed values:

my_module.settings:
  mapping:
    status:
      type: enum
      enum_class: '\Drupal\my_module\MyEnum'

If your code calls Drupal\Core\Config\FileStorageFactory::getSync() directly, switch to the service instead:

// Before:
$storage = FileStorageFactory::getSync();
// After:
$storage = \Drupal::service('config.storage.sync');

item.title: #3608184: Load multiple cardinality fields with a smaller result set
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 7 files, +191/−64 · php +191/−64
  • Diff: 35c7c09
  • Discussion: #3608184 · 7 contributors · 47 comments
  • Followers: 13

Summary

When an entity has several multi-value ("multiple cardinality") fields, Drupal core previously ran one query per field and then re-sorted the results in PHP. This change combines those queries into a single, more efficient query per chunk of fields, cutting down the number of database queries needed to load such entities. This is a purely internal performance optimization to entity loading. There is nothing for site owners or module developers to configure or change; Drupal's own performance tests recorded fewer queries on pages like the front page and node pages after this change.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

This is a follow-up to #3607938, which found that naively joining multiple multi-value field tables together in one query produces a cartesian product (a row for every combination of deltas across fields). This issue's fix, in SqlContentEntityStorage::loadMultipleCardinalityFields(), avoids that by building a "delta spine": a subselect that UNIONs the (entity_id, langcode, delta) rows from each dedicated field table in the chunk, giving the full set of valid delta combinations for the loaded entities. Each field's dedicated table is then LEFT JOINed onto that spine (aliased delta_join) matching on ID, langcode and delta, so every field's value lines up on the correct row without multiplying against other fields. When a chunk contains only one multiple-cardinality field, the union step is skipped entirely and the query selects straight from that field's table, since a single table can't multiply against itself.

loadFromDedicatedTables() now chunks the multiple-cardinality fields together (via array_chunk() using the same FIELD_MINIMUM_CHUNK_SIZE used for single-cardinality fields) and calls loadMultipleCardinalityFields() once per chunk instead of once per field, and the previous PHP-side ksort() re-sort of deltas is removed since the query now does ORDER BY on the delta from the spine. The method signature was reworked accordingly: the $base_query, $base_table, $base_id_key, and $base_langcode_alias parameters were dropped since the query is now built independently of the base entity query, and an $ids parameter was added to constrain the spine and field tables directly. EXPLAIN output shared in the issue confirmed the union/join query hits indexes on every branch, and Drupal's PerformanceTest suites were updated to reflect the reduced query counts (for example the Umami front page cold cache dropped from 184 to 178 queries, and the standard profile node page cold cache dropped from 204 to 195).

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: July 3, 2026
  • Committed: July 24, 2026 (20 days and 2 commits later)

Key contributors

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting, Inc.)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • godotislate
  • nicxvan (nLightened Development LLC)
  • scott_euser (Soapbox)

Collaboration

catch explored several alternatives before landing on this approach: a new database table pre-populated with sequential delta values to join against (rejected as "a bit painful" and hard to size for sites with very high cardinality), and separately ruled out UNION of the actual field data (column type mismatches), a temporary table, a MySQL sequence, and GROUP BY (no reliable delta to group on), documenting why each wouldn't work. alexpott then proposed building the delta spine from a UNION subselect of just the (id, langcode, delta) tuples instead of a physical table, and further simplified it to drop the join to the base entity table entirely. catch called this approach avoiding "the crime against databases" of the earlier table-based idea and moved the issue to RTBC. item.description:

  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +34/−0 · php +34
  • Diff: 478fb37
  • Discussion: #3569316 · 14 contributors · 41 comments

Summary

A fatal TypeError could occur during common content operations (saving or deleting nodes, flushing caches, language switches) on Drupal 11.3+, causing the cachetags table to not be updated and leaving caches permanently stale until manually rebuilt. The error was intermittent but reliably reproducible on PHP 8.4 and in multi-replica PHP-FPM setups. This fix ensures cache tag invalidation and all other post-transaction callbacks complete correctly on every request.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

PHP's object destruction order during request shutdown is undefined. If Connection::__destruct() executed before Transaction::__destruct(), the Connection would set its internal $this->connection PDO property to NULL. When Transaction::__destruct() subsequently ran purge() → processPostTransactionCallbacks(), any registered callback that used the database (such as DatabaseCacheTagsChecksum::rootTransactionEndCallback → doInvalidateTags()) would call Connection::prepareStatement() with a null PDO, throwing StatementWrapperIterator::__construct(): Argument #2 ($clientConnection) must be of type object, null given.

The fix adds a $this->processPostTransactionCallbacks() call at the end of TransactionManagerBase::commitAll(). commitAll() is already invoked during PHP shutdown via commitAllOnShutdown to unwind any open transaction stack. By also draining the post-transaction callback queue there, all callbacks execute while the Connection object is still fully initialized, before any destructors can run. The same pattern applies to any module that registers its own callbacks via TransactionManagerInterface::addPostTransactionCallback().

A new kernel test testPostTransactionsAlwaysExecutedBeforeConnectionIsDestroyed in TransactionTest verifies the scenario: it closes the connection and unsets the transaction in the same destructor-race order, then confirms the callback's side-effects are present after reopening the connection. A one-line PHPStan suppression comment (// @phpstan-ignore unset.possiblyHookedProperty) was removed from the test file in the 11.x and 11.4.x follow-up commits to pass static analysis. The related cleanup issue #3406985 (converting core transactions to explicit commitOrRelease()) was a related but separate effort and did not fix this callback-ordering problem.

item.description:

Summary

Drupal core now ships with Guzzle 8.0, upgraded from 7.x. The composer.json constraint is broadened to ^7.10 || ^8.0 (and guzzlehttp/psr7 to ^2.8.0 || ^3.0), so sites can still resolve Guzzle 7 when other dependencies force it. The installed lock file pins guzzlehttp/guzzle 8.0.0, guzzlehttp/psr7 3.0.0, and guzzlehttp/promises 3.0.0. The dev dependency php-http/guzzle7-adapter is removed because no Guzzle 8 compatible release exists for it.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Requirements: Guzzle 8.0.0, guzzlehttp/psr7 3.0.0, and guzzlehttp/promises 3.0.0 are now locked; core composer.json allows ^7.10 || ^8.0 for guzzle and ^2.8.0 || ^3.0 for psr7.

Technical details

The composer.json version constraints for guzzlehttp/guzzle and guzzlehttp/psr7 are widened to accept both major versions. ralouphie/getallheaders drops out of the lock file because guzzlehttp/psr7 3.x no longer depends on it.

Guzzle 8 removes ClientInterface::getConfig() entirely, so three PHPStan $ignoreErrors entries suppressing that deprecation warning (in BrowserTestBase, ClientFactoryTest, and DrupalTestBrowser) are deleted. In DrupalTestBrowser::doRequest(), the catch block previously caught RequestException and had to guard against a null response; Guzzle 8's BadResponseException (covering 4xx and 5xx responses) always carries a response, so the null-response branch and the old RequestException import are removed.

Guzzle 8 requires handler callables to return a PromiseInterface rather than a ResponseInterface directly. A mock handler in LocaleTranslationTest is updated to wrap its Response in Create::promiseFor() and declare the correct return type signature function(RequestInterface $request, array $options): PromiseInterface.

Guzzle 8's CookieJar no longer stores a Secure-flagged cookie received over a non-HTTPS connection (the HTTPS mock used in browser tests is not a real TLS connection). LoginHttpsTest::loginHttps() is updated to parse the Set-Cookie response header directly with SetCookie::fromString() instead of calling CookieJar::getCookieByName(). A companion fix in BrowserTestBase::getSessionCookies() guards against a null session ID before building the cookie jar.

Guzzle 8 also trims the trailing newline that earlier versions appended to the response body excerpt in exception messages, so several test string assertions drop the trailing \n.

Upgrade

Custom Guzzle handlers must return a PromiseInterface instead of a ResponseInterface:

// Before (Guzzle 7)
$handler = function (RequestInterface $request, array $options): ResponseInterface {
    return new Response(200, [], 'body');
};

// After (Guzzle 8)
use GuzzleHttp\Promise\Create;
use GuzzleHttp\Promise\PromiseInterface;

$handler = function (RequestInterface $request, array $options): PromiseInterface {
    return Create::promiseFor(new Response(200, [], 'body'));
};

Exception handling for 4xx/5xx responses should use BadResponseException instead of RequestException:

// Before (Guzzle 7)
use GuzzleHttp\Exception\RequestException;
catch (RequestException $e) {
    if (!$e->hasResponse()) {
        throw $e;
    }
    $response = $e->getResponse();
}

// After (Guzzle 8)
use GuzzleHttp\Exception\BadResponseException;
catch (BadResponseException $e) {
    $response = $e->getResponse();
}

Remove any calls to getConfig() on GuzzleHttp\Client or GuzzleHttp\ClientInterface; that method is removed in Guzzle 8. Store configuration values your code needs at construction time instead of reading them back from the client.
